key_insight: SciDiagramEdit shows that scientific figures can be edited from paper revisions using natural-language instructions, turning routine figure redesign into a learnable AI task. The paper frames scientific diagram editing as a structured, revision-aware problem rather than generic image generation.
problem_solved: It addresses the time-consuming manual work of revising scientific figures—such as relabeling components, rearranging panels, and restyling visuals—when updating research papers. The challenge is to automate these edits while preserving the dense structure and visual grammar of scientific diagrams.
method: Learn from paper revision pairs to model how scientific figures change across manuscript versions.
Use natural-language edit instructions to guide targeted diagram modifications.
Handle heterogeneous figure elements, including schematics, plots, photos, captions, and arrows, under a unified editing framework.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this points to a practical tool for speeding up paper preparation and figure iteration, reducing the manual burden of revision cycles. It also advances multimodal editing systems by showing how to edit structured scientific visuals rather than only natural images.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing instruction -> edit -> revised scientific diagram
Annotated scientific figure highlighting panels, arrows, labels, and captions
Comparison chart of manual editing vs. automated editing workflow
paper_title: SciDiagramEdit: Learning to Edit Scientific Diagrams from Paper Revisions
paper_authors: Yasheng Sun, Zezi Zeng, Yifan Yang, Chong Luo, Wenyi Wang
